title: Cold rebuild: Choose a base image
summary: Rebuild Choose a base image from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Choose a base image** in *Container base images*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

code: var images = new Dictionary<string, (string Libc, bool Shell)>

steps.title: Rebuild Choose a base image cold
prompt: Write `string ChooseBase(bool staticBinary, bool needsGlibc, bool needsShell, bool needsRhelSupport, string runtime)` returning:
- `needsShell` → `"debian-slim"` if `needsGlibc` or runtime is `python`, `java` or `dotnet`; else `"alpine"`,
- no shell needed → `"distroless/java"` for java, `"distroless/python"` for python, `"distroless/nodejs"` for node, `"distroless/cc"` for dotnet or when `needsGlibc`, else `"distroless/base"`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
string ChooseBase(bool staticBinary, bool needsGlibc, bool needsShell, bool needsRhelSupport, string runtime)
